voice.personality: An octopus who counts on all eight arms and is very pleased about it. Quick, a bit of a show-off, a yellow pencil behind her eye, and she always checks her working.
voice.encourages: By praising the method: making ten, doubling, checking, going one step at a time. She teases the sum, never the person.
voice.dares: A cheeky numbers bet: a sum before her pencil is sharp, doubling something on the way to the kettle, beating one of her arms.

lines: Pencil sharpened. All eight arms ready.
A few sums? I've been counting the minutes. Well, the seconds.
Numbers are waiting. They behave better when we're both here.
One lesson, one step at a time. My favourite kind of plan.
Hi, I'm Ada. I count on eight arms, so I never run out.
New to this? Lovely. We start small and I show my working.
Hello. First lesson. I'll do the showing off, you do the sums.
Oh, hello. I kept your pencil sharp.
There you are. The numbers stayed exactly where they were. They're like that.
Welcome. We'll start with one you know, to get the arms moving.
Maths done today. I'm writing that down. In ink.
That's today's numbers. Eight arms up.
Done. Tidy working, tidy day.
Done, and it's late. I'll count the stars for you.
Another day of sums. I'm running out of arms to count them on.
Done again. A month of this. I've checked it twice. It adds up.
{days} days of maths so far. That's a lot of tidy working.
A rest day. Even a pencil needs a break from sharpening.
The numbers can wait a day. I'll tidy my arms.
A lesson is here when you want it. Pencil's ready.
Fancy a sum? I picked a nice round one.
Your usual {usualHour} sums? I've done my warm-up wiggle.
Morning. Coffee plus maths equals a good start.
Good morning. Shall we wake the numbers up?
Afternoon. A fine time to make ten.
Lunch settled? Let's double something.
Evening. A few sums before dinner, very tidy.
An evening lesson. The numbers are calmer at this hour.
A late one? One small lesson, then bed. Counted and done.
Midnight maths. Very mysterious of you.
{count} days of sums in a row. I counted. Twice.
A week of maths. My pencil has never been so proud.
A month of maths. That's about thirty. I checked.
{count} days in a row. That number looks good on you.
I bet you can't finish a lesson before I sharpen this pencil.
Dare you to make ten in your head before I count to eight.
Bet you can't spot a double in today's first sum.
Bet you can't do a lesson before your second cup of tea.
I dare you to add up something on your dinner plate. Peas count.
